column3: MT 3:33. “It burned to him” is rendered “he became furious.”

MT 3:34. “The army of Samaria” is rendered “the wealthy men of Samaria.” The questions are terse in Hebrew; NASB supplies “it,” and “restore the stones” is rendered “revive the stones.” The meaning of several phrases is uncertain.
MT 3:35. “Go up” is rendered “jump on.”
MT 3:36. “We are contempt” is rendered “how we are despised.”
MT 3:37. “Cover over” is rendered “forgive.” “Provoked to anger before the builders” is rendered “demoralized the builders.”
MT 3:38. “To its middle” is rendered “to half its height,” and “a heart” as “a mind.”
MT 4:1. “The repair … had gone up” is rendered “the repair … went on”; “it burned to them” is rendered “they were very angry.”
MT 4:2. “Confusion” is rendered “a disturbance.”
MT 4:3. Close to the Hebrew.
MT 4:4. “Judah said” is rendered “in Judah it was said”; NASB sets the saying as poetry and adds “Yet.”
MT 4:5. “Opponents” is rendered “enemies.”
MT 4:6. The Hebrew is difficult; NASB supplies “They will come up against us,” and the meaning is uncertain.
MT 4:7. “In the open places” is rendered “the exposed places,” and “to clans” as “in families.” NASB supplies “men.”
MT 4:8. NASB supplies “their fear”; “fight on” is rendered “fight for.”
MT 4:9. “Purpose” is rendered “plan.”
MT 4:10. “My young men” is rendered “my servants,” and “body armor” as “breastplates.”
MT 4:11. “Carrying in the burden were carrying” is rendered “took their load.”
MT 4:12. “The one who gave a blast on the ram's horn” is rendered “the trumpeter.”
MT 4:13. “Each from his brother” is rendered “from one another.”
MT 4:14. “Ram's horn” is rendered “trumpet,” and “assemble to us” as “rally to us.”
MT 4:15. “When the dawn came up” is rendered “from dawn.”
MT 4:16. “The day work” is rendered “a laborer by day.”
MT 4:17. “Each one his weapon the water” is rendered “each took his weapon even to the water”; the Hebrew is obscure, and the meaning is uncertain.
